title: In two adult fly eyes, columnar synapse counts vary 3 to 6 times more than Poisson; spatial, column and cell factors explain all of the excess in the male CNS and all but a 9% edge-specific CV in FAFB
abstract: Question: when the same connection occurs many times, which part of its synapse count variation is specific to each connection? A prior SCI study found that two copies of homologous fly connections vary more than Poisson sampling, and that the excess increases with strength. With two copies it could not find the cause. Approach: the fly optic lobe has about 800 columns with one cell of each columnar type. We used column-assigned cells in both eyes of FlyWire FAFB v783 (female; Princeton and Buhmann synapse tables) and of the male CNS v1.0. This gave 64 to 206 connection types and 55,519 to 147,087 copies per eye. Covariances between different copies are free of Poisson noise. We used them to split the extra-Poisson variance into a spatial trend, a column factor, factors for each presynaptic and postsynaptic cell, and an edge-specific rest, with block-bootstrap intervals. Results: for type means of 16 or more synapses, phi around the type mean was 3.3 and 3.9 (male) and 5.2 and 5.9 (FAFB). Pairs of distant columns reproduced the rising two-copy curve of the central brain. Pairs of neighbouring male columns gave phi of 1.3 to 2.0 at all counts. In the male CNS, after a cubic spatial trend, the edge-specific variance was -0.0018 (95% interval -0.0029 to -0.0003) and 0.0020 (0.0001 to 0.0041) in CV squared units, so the edge-specific CV is at most about 6%. With identical type pairs, FAFB had 2.1 to 2.5 times the male excess and an edge-specific CV of about 9%. The Princeton and Buhmann tables shared the Princeton excess almost completely, so it is not detector noise. Type means agreed within 7 to 10% between the eyes of one animal, but differed by 30 to 38% between animals and by 40% between the two synapse tables of one eye. Limitations: two animals of different sex, imaging and reconstruction pipeline; columnar types only; additive-variance approximation.
